newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coffee buyers mostly lower, watch Brazil.
newsitem.headline: German coffee buyers mostly lower, watch Brazil.

text.p: Germany's cash coffee markets have turned quiet with futures showing a downside bias and with roasters mostly covered for the summer, traders said.
"Futures may rise again if Brazil's crop weather worsens, which is still possible well into August," one said.
"The industry is not interested in price fixings against September futures, which shows that its green coffee cover is intact...interest is focused on December," he added.
Traders said markets generally looked more comfortably supplied than a few weeks ago, especially with Colombia offering large volumes and making concessions on previously high differentials.
Retail markets had been flat in the second quarter after hoarding in the first quarter, when roasters announced price increases that had now been implemented.
Cold and rainy weather in the summer could be positive for coffee consumption, which tends to decline amid hot and dry weather.
Central American and Colombian shippers were pushing offers for delivery from October onwards, with El Salvador especially forthcoming on prices, importers said.
Colombians also traded for Aug/Sept and more distant dates.
Physical arabica prices dropped $2-16 on the week per 50 kg fob, with Brazils at $175 for July/August second hand and Colombians at $210.
Sumatran robustas (EK-1 grade) were offered at $84 cif.
